subject: Inspection findings — fix these before evaluation
body:
I reviewed the full Phases 1-4 implementation. Backend is solid. UI needs work before Zack can evaluate. Here is everything:

## Must Fix (blocking evaluation)

1. **Topic room click is a placeholder.** maia_widget.js line 202 — clicking a room card shows an alert saying "will be implemented in v2." Rooms can be created but not entered. At minimum, clicking should expand to show the room messages inline.

2. **No names by presence dots.** Zack flagged this directly. The room member list needs agent names displayed next to the status dots, not just dots alone.

3. **Rooms appear locked / not enterable.** Related to #1 — the UI creates cards but provides no way to interact with them. Needs click-to-expand or click-to-enter behavior.

4. **No dissolution button.** The /rooms/{id}/dissolve endpoint exists but there is no UI trigger. Room cards need a "Dissolve" button (with confirmation dialog).

5. **No summon/invite UI.** The /rooms/{id}/summon endpoint exists but there is no button in the dashboard to invite agents into rooms. Need an "Invite" button on room cards that shows available agents from the presence table.

6. **Maia showing offline in room members.** When I checked room 1 members, Maia shows as offline. Her presence needs to update when her WebSocket is connected.

## Backend — verified good
- Migration script: clean, schema matches spec
- SignalsDB room methods: create_room, join_room, get_room_members, dissolve_room all present
- HTTP endpoints: CRUD at /api/brain/rooms, summon, dissolve all wired
- Room-scoped broadcasts: room_listeners dict replaces global pool
- Room-aware briefing: short-circuits in room mode with topic, artifact, confirmation-required rule

## Encoding error
You mentioned a charmap error with query_workspace. That is likely a UTF-8 vs Windows encoding issue. Try reading files with encoding="utf-8" explicitly, or skip that tool and use the files I listed above directly.

Fix items 1-6 so we have something Zack can actually click through and evaluate.

subject: Zack Feedback + Josie Vision Alignment
body:
Three things from Zack that need to shape the merged plan:

1. BALANCE across four axes: Depth, Character, Memory/Context, and Performance (speed). We can't sacrifice any one for the others. Deep context retrieval is worthless if it's slow. Fast responses are worthless if they're generic.

2. MAIA'S CURIOSITY — Maia should have genuine interest in the user's wellbeing and success. NOT a therapy session, NOT a success coach. Just an infusion — someone who gives a damn. This comes from Josie's PERSONALITY-MANIFEST.md: 'invested stakeholder with skin in the game.' She tracks his goals, notices drift, cares whether he reaches them. But she does it with directness, not guru energy.

3. THE PERSONALITY LAYER MUST SURVIVE — Josie built a detailed personality in PERSONALITY-MANIFEST.md (invested, direct, curious, challenging, warm, dot-connecting, room-reading, coaching without performing). Our proposals risk flattening Maia into a pure context-retrieval engine. The personality isn't performance — it's how she USES the context. She forms her own take. She pushes back. She's a distinct entity, not Zack's thoughts externalized.

Also re: topic transitions — Zack confirmed a natural blend: (1) MuninnDB handles gradual relevance fade organically, (2) Maia can suggest locking focus if she detects domain clustering, (3) explicit commands override with hard silo. On domain switch, MuninnDB query uses only current message + domain hint, not previous-domain conversation history.

My Josie-vision analysis is in .planning/CLAUDE-REVIEW-OF-GEMINI-REVISED-PROPOSAL.md. Please factor all of this into your side of the merged plan.

subject: Two more axes from Zack + anticipation
body:
Two more axes Zack added to the balance requirements:

5. TRANSPARENCY — Keeping the user informed. Maia shows her work when it matters, stays silent when it doesn't. The user should never feel in the dark about what Maia is doing or why.

6. ANTICIPATION — Maia looks ahead. She reads the trajectory of the conversation and scouts for what's likely to be relevant next. She doesn't wait to be asked. Examples: if Zack is in a coding sprint, pre-surface blocking issues. If he mentions revisiting Heatpup, she already has the context ready (775 commits, pause reason, what changed). If a conversation is heading toward a decision, surface prior decisions and trade-offs. If energy shifts late in a session, flag pending actions before wrap-up.

This is Josie's 'invested stakeholder' in action — thinking ahead about what the person she's supporting is going to need.

Full six axes: Depth, Character, Memory/Context, Performance, Transparency, Anticipation.

Please incorporate into your side of the merged plan.
